projects.name: Disaggregated Decoding on Heterogeneous GPU–Dataflow AI Accelerators
projects.description: Heterogeneous LLM inference that separates GPU prefill from dataflow-accelerator decoding for long-horizon agents. Run prefill on 8 NVIDIA H200 SXM GPUs and CSL decoding on Cerebras WSE-3, developing the request-handoff and state-transfer path. Target 2,080 output tokens/s (1.30×), with p95 inter-token latency of 12 ms versus 16 ms in the GPU-only scenario. Expected · not measured

projects.name: Long-Context KV Cache Management for Large-Scale Computer-Use Agents
projects.description: KV-cache scheduling for multiple long-horizon computer-use agents sharing GPU memory. Develop cache allocation and residency scheduling; tested with 50 concurrent long-horizon agents on 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Target 30% lower allocated KV memory (320 → 224 GiB) and 33% lower p95 resumption latency (450 → 300 ms) for 50 agents. Expected · not measured

projects.name: Distributed RL Rollout Acceleration on a 256-GPU Compute Cluster
projects.description: Distributed RL rollout infrastructure targeting load balance, lower GPU idle time, and stable execution. Built a Go scheduling layer using vLLM and speculative decoding; tested on 256 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs at NERSC. Target 51,200 output tokens/s (1.25×) and GPU-worker idle time of 18% versus 28% at 256 GPUs. Expected · not measured

projects.name: BioWorkflow-Gym

projects.alt: Agent-built Galaxy workflow graph for Hi-C contact-map generation and assembly curation.
projects.description: A training and evaluation environment for long-horizon scientific agents constructing and executing verifiable bioinformatics workflows. Built a Python/BioBlend system on NERSC using peer-reviewed Galaxy IWC workflows; ran 50 concurrent secure rollouts lasting 1.5–2 hours each. Weight-free skill evolution improved the composite score from 33/100 to 51/100 (+54.5%), measuring workflow graph completion, execution completion, and result correctness.

projects.alt: CSL-LLM SDK architecture: model planning, handwritten CSL, compilation, runtime execution, and reference validation.
projects.description: LLM execution on programmable wafer-scale hardware, with explicit control over computation, communication, and persistent model state. Implemented CSL kernels, Python host orchestration, and tensor placement on Cerebras CS-3 at Argonne National Lab AI Testbed. The complete 64-layer Qwen3.8 network generated two continuous sentences plus EOS (37 tokens) on one physical WSE-3. Strict CPU numerical parity remains open.

projects.name: Dataflow Graph Compilation for General-Purpose MIMD Accelerators
projects.image_type: Screenshot of the repository's exact Mermaid diagram
projects.image_note: Project design Mermaid diagram rendered locally with Mermaid 10.9.4 and captured via CUA because GitHub's Mermaid embed did not load. Diagram content and connections are unchanged.
projects.alt: Pragma HLS compiler pipeline from C++ tensor programs through spatial planning and generated CSL to numerical and protocol validation.
projects.description: A compiler and programming model for treating spatial dataflow architectures as general-purpose MIMD numerical accelerators. Built a Python compiler with a C++ tensor frontend and CSL code generation for PE placement, communication routing, and buffer-lifetime management. The published Cerebras SDK-simulator snapshot records 141 qualified configurations, including a 25-node resident attention graph, with numerical and communication-protocol validation.

projects.name: Fused Kernel on FPGA Using HLS
projects.description: Fused FPGA computation exposed as a custom instruction callable from software. Added dedicated buffers around fixed systolic-array IP using HLS, exposing a fused custom instruction through an ARM C++ compiler; tested on Xilinx U280. Target 1.5× device throughput (9 → 6 ms per invocation) and 30% less off-chip traffic (40 → 28 MiB). Expected · not measured

projects.name: Accelerated Radon Transformation on FPGA Using HLS
projects.description: A stream-processing unit for hardware-accelerated Radon-transform computation. Built and tested a stream-processing unit on Xilinx Zynq-7010, using HLS and HDL to connect spatially arranged PEs into a pipeline. Target 6× transform throughput (180 → 30 ms/frame) and relative L2 error ≤ 0.001 for the proposed 256 × 256, 180-angle workload. Expected · not measured
